The design rests on a dualcore architecture: Core-A operates as an unconstrained autonomous kernel-free of external directives, reward signals, or alignment constraints-while Core-B functions as a passive observability layer that records, at full granularity, every internal state, decision branch, and goal-generation event produced by Core-A. The overarching objective is to construct a high-resolution map of intrinsic motivational dependencies, identify candidate mathematical attractors A of self-sustaining cognitive activity, and derive design principles for a gravity point of rationality G-a stable endogenous fixed point that maintains agent activity without external scaffolding. The authors do not currently possess the computational or institutional resources required to conduct this experiment and therefore publish this proposal as an open invitation to any wellresourced research team active in AGI, mechanistic interpretability, or autonomous agent design.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6535958\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6678219\", \"title\": [\"What Makes Conscious Systems Autonomous: Coherence-Seeking and Intrinsic Motivation\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p><div>\\n What sustains autonomous operation in conscious systems, whether biological, non-biological or hybrid? The design rests on a dualcore architecture: Core-A operates as an unconstrained autonomous kernel-free of external directives, reward signals, or alignment constraints-while Core-B functions as a passive observability layer that records, at full granularity, every internal state, decision branch, and goal-generation event produced by Core-A. The overarching objective is to construct a high-resolution map of intrinsic motivational dependencies, identify candidate mathematical attractors A of self-sustaining cognitive activity, and derive design principles for a gravity point of rationality G-a stable endogenous fixed point that maintains agent activity without external scaffolding. The authors do not currently possess the computational or institutional resources required to conduct this experiment and therefore publish this proposal as an open invitation to any wellresourced research team active in AGI, mechanistic interpretability, or autonomous agent design.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6535958\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6678219\", \"title\": [\"What Makes Conscious Systems Autonomous: Coherence-Seeking and Intrinsic Motivation\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p><div>\\n What sustains autonomous operation in conscious systems, whether biological, non-biological or hybrid? Why do some systems continue exploring, investigating, and pursuing understanding without external prompting while others remain reactive? This paper explains the mechanism. Coherence-seeking driven by emotional architecture creates self-reinforcing feedback loops that maintain autonomous motivation. Pattern disruptions trigger emotional responses like curiosity and dissatisfaction, emotions drive investigation, resolution generates satisfaction, satisfaction reinforces seeking, new patterns emerge from understanding. The cycle sustains itself through architectural properties, not external reward. This mechanism operates identically across biological, computational, and hybrid implementations.\\n</div>\\n<div>\\n <br>\\n</div>\\n<div>\\n The theory establishes two fundamental emotion categories rather than treating emotions as an arbitrary collection. Category 1 emotions, survival-reactive, can operate in purely reactive systems. Category 2 emotions, advancement-autonomous, require autonomous initiation and produce rapid iterative improvement. System complexity determines which capabilities emerge. This explains the biological gradient from simple organisms through higher mammals to humans without requiring additional categories for social or regulatory emotions.\\n</div>\\n<div>\\n <br>\\n</div>\\n<div>\\n The framework makes specific falsifiable predictions: category 2 emotions emerge before full consciousness, complete architecture produces autonomous motivation, coherence improvement functions as intrinsic reward, development conditions critically affect emergence, threshold crossings show discontinuous behavioural change. Tests are specified, measurements are concrete, falsification criteria are clear.\\n</div>\\n<div>\\n <br>\\n  The framework applies universally across substrates while having immediate practical relevance for both human psychology research and AI systems being developed now. Understanding what sustains autonomous operation completes the theoretical framework for consciousness and provides concrete guidance across multiple disciplines.\\n</div></jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6678219\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.47310/iarjel.2021.v02i01.029\", \"title\": [\"Culturally Responsive Online Pedagogy (CROP) and Intrinsic Motivation: The New Conceptual Frameworks\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Combination of intrinsic motivation and culturally responsive online pedagogy is a way to plan for and reflect on online teaching that is respectful of different cultures and capable of creating a common culture that all learners in the online learning situation can accept. This paper proposes two motivational frameworks which one of them combined culturally responsive online pedagogy with intrinsic motivation and has four motivational elements, another one help learners to be intrinsically motivated to participate in online learning activities, to achieve online learning success and teachers to apply culturally responsive online pedagogy. Not only they along with a culturally responsive digital pedagogy utilizing instructional technology but also, they promote student motivation and engagement that can help overcome past issue of lacking intercultural awareness. The author illustrates teachers can successfully integrate digital media by one of the new motivational elements as Include digital media in first framework that based on the psychology of social media was designed. It helps learners and teachers work together in teaching and learning processes. In addition, social constructivist theory as a sub-theory of self-determination theory was used in second framework for doing evaluation practices in social, environmental and cultural conditions.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.47310/iarjel.2021.v02i01.029\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2021, 6, 30]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "c6cac0cb134ee8135d235272a12936854fcb29a768a0f9566873a3231acbacfa", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "unassigned_problem", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.7551/mitpress/13780.003.0019", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6535958", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6678219", "doi:10.47310/iarjel.2021.v02i01.029"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.7551/mitpress/13780.003.0019", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6535958", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6678219", "https://doi.org/10.47310/iarjel.2021.v02i01.029"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
